messages.author: 3451c2e31f1fe160
messages.subject: secrlinear GoF testing
parts:
I think I probably know the answer to this, but figured I'd ask the hive mind anyways: Has GoF testing similar to secr.fit() been implemented yet for secrlinear with a linear mask and user-defined network distances? 

I've attempted to apply secr.fit() to a model with a linear mask and network distance function, but receive the following error:

Error in attr(session.mask, "miscparm") <- coef(object)[miscindx, 1] : attempt to set an attribute on NULL.

This makes me think that the linear mask is not recognized.

Thanks,
-Sean

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: secrlinear GoF testing
parts:
Hi Sean
I assume we are talking here about secr.test(). I don't remember specifically implementing that for linear data, but it might be interesting to pin down where it comes adrift and whether it is easily fixed. The error you are getting comes from sim.detect() that is called by simulate.secr() early in a call to secr.test(). I'll try to check it in the next day or so. If the worst comes to the worst you can replicate the behaviour of secr.test easily enough by simulating your own linear data via sim.linearpopn and sim.capthist (see secrlinear-vignette.pdf).
Murray
